units.function: Paperclip's per-Agent Skill assignment experience: search the company Skill library, distinguish desired managed Skills from adapter-detected read-only Skills, autosave replacement selections, optionally pin the core Skill to seeded beta releases and present source metadata.
units.dependencyDirection: Five UI/helper modules and four narrow unit tests depend on Agent/company-Skill/instance-setting APIs, shared Agent/Skill types, adapter labels, Agent-specific state reconciliation and generic UI primitives. The main tab directly embeds Paperclip core-Skill and vendor adapter branches, while the row/filter/source helpers remain comparatively low-coupled.
units.keyDataModels: Agent desired Skill keys or key/versionId entries, company Skill library/list/version records, runtime-detected Skill entries, persistent/ephemeral/unsupported materialization mode, version-pin map, stale desired keys and source display metadata.
units.lifecycle: Fetch Agent Skill snapshot, company library and beta setting; hydrate draft/pins; derive enabled/available/detected/stale projections; debounce replace-mode autosave after toggles; immediately save release-pin changes; report saved/error state; runtime materializes desired Skills on the next run.
units.testAssessment: Four focused Vitest files passed 23/23 tests on 2026-08-19, and a no-emit/non-incremental UI TypeScript check passed. Tests cover release label/date fallbacks, beta-gated payload pins, case-insensitive metadata filtering and privacy-preserving source labels. They do not mount the tab/row, exercise API convergence/races, auth/tenant scope, unsupported adapters, merge/replace effects, stale removal, content/provenance integrity, release compatibility, runtime materialization, errors, accessibility/mobile behavior or approval/evidence semantics.
units.designRationale: Give operators a compact per-Agent view that separates company-managed desired Skills from runtime-discovered unmanaged Skills, supports adapter-specific materialization modes and offers an experimental frozen release for the core Paperclip Skill.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs governed capability/training assignment where a human understands the exact Skill digest, source/license, requested tools/data, compatibility/certification and risk; the Connector must attest what was actually materialized for a specific execution rather than treating desired UI state as truth.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT only the low-coupling row, search and privacy-preserving source-display patterns plus the desired-versus-detected projection. Replace AgentSkillsTab orchestration with a versioned SkillAssignmentPlan: immutable content digest, Connector capability check, explicit merge semantics, policy/approval for consequential changes, optimistic concurrency, staged effective state and runtime attestation. Keep training/certification records separate from runtime Skill packages.
units.responsibilityConflict: Skill enable/remove and release changes alter the Agent's next-run instructions but autosave like preferences, with no accountable human, reason, permission/data impact, risk class, approval digest or immutable receipt. 'Saved' means desired state reached an API, not that the Connector materialized or executed the approved bytes.

securityFindings: Desired Skill selection changes next-run instructions yet is debounced/autosaved without impact preview, accountable-human approval, action digest or immutable audit receipt.
The live default is labeled recommended and may drift; only one Paperclip-specific beta Skill exposes version pins, and no content digest, source commit, compatibility or certification is shown.
Disabling the global beta flag causes subsequent saves to omit retained version pins, potentially moving Agents silently from frozen releases to live content.
Replace-mode saves and immediate release saves have no visible revision/CAS token; concurrent toggles, pin changes or another operator can overwrite state.
Vendor-specific ACP/OpenClaw branches leak adapter types into generic product logic rather than consuming Connector capability declarations and stable reasons.
Source labels reduce filesystem disclosure but are only display strings; provenance omits digest, commit, license, signer, scan, trust and revocation state.
Stale desired Skills are removable with one click and otherwise remain desired; there is no server admission policy proving whether execution is blocked, degraded or still using cached bytes.
'Saved' reports desired-state API success, not Connector acknowledgment or runtime attestation of the exact materialized Skill bundle.
Raw mutation error messages are rendered; stable error codes and structured remediation are absent.
The focused tests exercise pure helpers only and do not cover the consequential component, API lifecycle or accessibility/mobile interactions.
